key_insight: Eu$_5$In$_2$As$_6$ shows magnetoresistive memory in the paramagnetic phase, meaning its resistivity depends on both magnetic-field strength and field history.
engineering_relevance: This points to a new nonvolatile sensing/memory mechanism for spintronic and quantum-device architectures that operates above the magnetic ordering temperature.
method: Measured resistivity under applied magnetic fields
Compared field magnitude versus field-history dependence
Analyzed temperature, field, and time dependence near and above the antiferromagnetic transition
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that magnetoresistive memory onsets at about twice the antiferromagnetic transition temperature, with resistivity showing clear temperature-, field-, and time-dependent behavior.
watch_item: The mechanism is not yet established and may rely on hidden order or short-range correlations, so device stability and reproducibility remain unresolved.
paper_title: Magnetoresistive Memory in the Paramagnetic Phase of Eu$_5$In$_2$As$_6$
